BLEEDING_AFTER_PREGNANCY_SUMMARY.target:
Bleeding after pregnancy, also known as lochia, is any bleeding that happens after a pregnancy. This kind of bleeding is expected and may last for several weeks.
While bleeding after pregnancy is common, heavy bleeding after pregnancy is not. Call your doctor or care team today if you experience heavy bleeding, or have bleeding and feel dizzy or light headed.

MENSTRUAL_CYCLE_DEVIATION_IRREGULAR_SUMM.target:
An irregular cycle is defined as at least a seventeen day difference between your shortest and longest cycles over the last six months. Persistent irregular cycles may be a sign of an underlying condition such as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), thyroid disease or menopausal transition.
Cycle Tracking can detect irregular cycles using your tracked flow days.

SYMPTOM_CHILLS_SUMMARY.target:
Chills is the sensation of being cold without an apparent reason.
Sometimes chills can be associated with shivering, particularly in the case of an accompanying infection. Shivering is an involuntary reflex consisting of very fast contraction and relaxation of muscles. It may be a sign that your immune system is trying to use heat to kill off the bacteria or virus causing the infection. This is why fever, chills, and shivering often happen together.
Chills can also be due to a severe drop in blood sugar, changes in your hormone production related to menopause, or an under-active thyroid.

TACHYCARDIA_SUMMARY.target:
An elevated heart rate while you’re not active may indicate important changes in your health.
Resting heart rates for adults typically fall between 50-100 beats per minutes. Heart rates in children are often higher than adults but decrease as they get older.
Apple Watch can check your heart rate and notify you when it detects a heart rate that’s above a selected threshold for 10 minutes. You can manage these notifications in Heart settings in the Apple Watch app.

SYMPTOM_SORE_THROAT_SUMMARY.target:
A sore throat is generally characterized as pain with a raw, burning, or scratchy sensation. It typically occurs when throat tissues or the tonsils become inflamed or dry up. It’s sometimes accompanied by sore and swollen neck glands, redness or white patches on the tonsils, a hoarse voice, or difficulty swallowing.
Usually, a sore throat is a symptom of a viral infection like a cold or a bacterial infection like strep throat (streptococcus). Viral infections generally go away on their own, while bacterial infections require treatment with antibiotics.
A sore throat can also be caused by allergies, acid reflux, inhaled irritants, prolonged shouting, or in rare cases a more serious condition like a cancerous tumor in the throat.

MENSTRUAL_CYCLE_DEVIATION_SPOTTING_SUMMA.target: Persistent spotting, also known as irregular intermenstrual bleeding, is defined as spotting that occurs in at least two of your cycles in the last six months. SYMPTOM_RAPID_POUNDING_OR_FLUTTERING_HEA.target:
Also known as palpitations, this type of change in the heartbeat is most often caused by strenuous activity, a stressful situation, a medication, or a stimulant like caffeine or alcohol. It can also be caused by hormonal changes associated with menstruation, pregnancy, or menopause.
Sometimes heart palpitations signal a more serious problem like a thyroid disorder or a heart condition like arrhythmia.
Medical assistance should be sought right away if palpitations are frequent or increasingly severe, or if accompanied by symptoms like chest pain, dizziness, or difficulty breathing.

SYMPTOM_DIZZINESS_SUMMARY.target:
Dizziness is feeling faint or lightheaded, often with difficulty balancing or a spinning sensation. Intensity and length can vary, from a momentary spell to a constant and debilitating state.
Some common causes of dizziness are dehydration, migraines, intoxication, low blood sugar, low blood pressure, and conditions that affect either the inner ear or the part of the brain that governs balance.
Sudden, severe, recurrent, or prolonged dizziness can be a sign of an urgent health issue. The same is true if it’s accompanied by other symptoms like a bad headache, chest pain, difficulty breathing, impaired vision, irregular heartbeat, disorientation, or nausea.

ACTIVITY_SUMMARY_SUMMARY.target:
Activity rings give you a quick visual reference of how active you are each day. When you complete your daily goal, its ring closes.
iPhone tracks your activity with a Move ring which measures the number of active calories you burn.
In addition to a Move ring, Apple Watch tracks activity with Exercise and Stand rings. Exercise measures how many minutes of brisk activity you do. Stand measures how often you stand up and move around throughout the day.

WALKING_SPEED_SUMMARY.target:
Walking speed represents how quickly you walk on flat ground. Walking speeds may be associated with how well you move overall and your physical abilities.
Walking requires strength, coordination, and aerobic fitness. Changes in any of these can affect your walking speed. Walking speed tends to slow down as you get older but sudden decreases may indicate a change in your health.
Your iPhone can record walking speed automatically when you carry your phone near your waist—such as in a pocket—and walk steadily on flat ground. To ensure accuracy, check that your height is up to date in Body Measurements.
Walking Speed is not recorded if your Wheelchair status is set to on.

SYMPTOM_WHEEZING_SUMMARY.target:
Wheezing is characterized by a high-pitched whistling sound made when inhaling or exhaling. It’s usually associated with difficulty breathing brought on by the inflammation and constriction of the airways.
Common causes include: respiratory conditions like asthma, emphysema, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); respiratory infections like the flu, pneumonia, or allergic reactions. In rare cases, wheezing can signal other serious conditions like lung cancer or heart failure.
If your wheezing is concerning, doesn’t go away, or keeps coming back, it should be discussed with a doctor. Emergency help should be sought if wheezing is severe, or if there’s reason to believe it’s caused by an allergic reaction or other urgent condition.

SPIROMETRY_FEV1_SUMMARY.target: Forced expiratory volume, 1 second, measures how much air you can force out of your lungs during the first second of a forced exhaled breath.

SYMPTOM_LOSS_OF_SMELL_SUMMARY.target:
Loss of smell is the inability to distinguish odors. Partial or complete loss of the sense of smell is a common effect of aging. It also often results from the swelling of nasal passages caused by a cold, flu or other infection. Other causes include allergies like hay fever, smoking, a deviated septum, or a polyp or tumor blocking the nasal passages.
An injury or disease that affects the part of the brain that processes odor can also lead to loss of smell. Less common causes include the use of certain medications and radiation therapy.
Those with an impaired sense of smell will experience a corresponding decrease in the ability to taste, finding it difficult to distinguish specific flavors.
Loss of smell caused by tissue damage or severe infection can be permanent. But if the cause is a temporary condition, smell usually returns within a few days.

SYMPTOM_HOT_FLASHES_SUMMARY.target:
Hot flashes are sudden feelings of warmth in the upper body not caused by external factors like weather, spicy food, or fever. They’re often accompanied by flushed skin, an increase in heart rate, and sweating. Hot flashes don’t actually change the body’s temperature and are not associated with fever.
A common effect of hormonal changes, hot flashes are considered a key indicator of menopause. However, not everyone who’s in menopause experiences them.
The effects are usually mild, but can be intense enough to disrupt sleep and daily activities.

FITZPATRICK_SKIN_TYPE_SUMMARY.target: The Fitzpatrick scale is a rating of your skin type, based on your skin’s tendency to burn and your skin’s ability to tan. The scale ranges from skin type I (always burns, never tans) to skin type VI (never burns, no change in appearance when tan).

TOOTHBRUSHING_EVENT_SUMMARY.target:
This represents the minutes you spend each day brushing your teeth. It’s recommended to brush twice a day for two minutes each time. Brushing your teeth properly can prevent tooth decay and support your overall oral health.

PROTEIN_SUMMARY.target:
Protein is critical for your body to function properly. Among other things, proteins create and maintain your muscles, organs, and much of the body’s other tissues. The word protein comes from the Greek word protos, which means “first” or “of prime importance.”
Proteins are made of smaller molecules called amino acids. The body produces most amino acids all by itself, but we must get some of them from our diet. Most foods contain at least some protein; good sources include meat, fish, eggs, dairy products, nuts, seeds, and legumes.

MENSTRUATION_SUMMARY.target: Menstruation is normal bleeding from the uterus that happens about every month. Also called period, menstruation is considered a vital sign. Tracking it can help you understand when your next period is likely to start and track changes in your cycles.

CYCLING_FUNCTIONAL_THRESHOLD_POWER_SUMMA.target:
Cycling Functional Threshold Power (FTP) is an estimate of the maximum average power you can sustain for 60 minutes while riding a bike. It is measured in watts (W). Your FTP can be affected by your height, age, weight, and level of fitness. It is frequently used to provide a rider with their power training zones and to help monitor progress.
Apple Watch can log your estimated cycling FTP automatically after a cycling workout. FTP is validated for users 20 and older.

SYMPTOM_NAUSEA_SUMMARY.target: Nausea is a feeling of sickness in your stomach that may lead to vomiting. There are many potential causes of nausea such as indigestion, infection, migraine, pregnancy, severe pain, or motion sickness. Rest, hydration, and starting with bland foods can help you recover.

SYMPTOM_BLADDER_INCONTINENCE_SUMMARY.target:
Bladder incontinence is the leaking of urine caused by loss of bladder control. It can range from an urgent need to pee to occasional leaks when coughing, laughing, or sneezing.
This can restrict activity and social interaction, and also signal a urinary tract infection or health issue in the bladder.
Incontinence often occurs with age because the bladder muscle weakens over time. Women can experience incontinence after menopause or childbirth, and it can be a symptom of prostate conditions in men. Other causes include certain types of surgery, as well as neurological disorders like multiple sclerosis or Parkinson’s.

SYMPTOM_CHEST_TIGHTNESS_OR_PAIN_SUMMARY.target:
Chest discomfort can take many forms. It may feel like squeezing, a weight on the chest, or difficulty breathing. There can be a burning sensation, a stabbing pain localized in one spot, or a diffused pain radiating out to other body parts.
The causes of chest tightness and pain range in seriousness from a strained muscle to a heart attack. Some specific signs of a heart attack include severe pressure, burning, or pain in the center of the chest; pain or numbness in the arms or upper body; and sudden nausea, shortness of breath, or cold sweats.
Other potential causes of chest discomfort include respiratory infection, asthma, anxiety, gastrointestinal conditions like acid reflux, pulmonary conditions, or strained muscles in the chest or torso.

WALKING_ASYMMETRY_PERCENTAGE_SUMMARY.target:
In a healthy walking pattern, the timing of the steps you take with each foot are very similar. Walking asymmetry is the percent of time that your steps with one foot are faster or slower than the other foot. This means the lower the percentage of asymmetry, the healthier your walking pattern.
Uneven walking patterns, such as limping, can be a sign of disease, injury, or other health issues. An even or symmetrical walk is often an important physical therapy goal when recovering from injury.
Your iPhone can record walking asymmetry automatically when you carry your phone near your waist—such as in a pocket—and walk steadily on flat ground.

LACTATION_SUMMARY.target:
Lactation is the production of milk from the breasts to feed an infant, either directly from the breast or from a bottle through the use of pumping or hand expressing.
It’s normally triggered by hormones during the final months of pregnancy, and production increases within the first 2-3 days after giving birth. This is often referred to as milk “coming in.” Lactation can also be induced with medication.
People can generally keep producing milk for as long as breastfeeding, pumping, or hand expression continues. Without these practices, production decreases and eventually stops within a few weeks.
The return of menstrual periods after pregnancy is often delayed by several months for people who are lactating.

PHQ9_SUMMARY.target:
Depression risk refers to an individual’s risk level for depression-related mental health conditions. This reflects the risk at the time of the most recent mental health assessment score using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). The PHQ-9 is a test many doctors use to help screen and measure the symptoms of depression over a two week period. A mental health questionnaire can help you find out more about what’s impacting your mental health.
Depression is one of the most common and treatable mental health conditions. Many factors, including family history, significant life changes, or environment, can impact an individual’s depression risk. Your risk score is not a diagnosis of any condition. If you have any questions about your mental health, you should bring them up with a doctor. You can learn more about your current risk for depression by taking a mental health questionnaire in Health.

ACTIVE_ENERGY_SUMMARY.target: This is an estimate of energy burned over and above your Resting Energy use (see Resting Energy). CALCIUM_SUMMARY.target: Calcium is a mineral found in many foods. Almost all calcium in your body is stored in bones and teeth to help make and keep them strong. Your body needs calcium to help muscles and blood vessels contract and expand, and to send messages through the nervous system. Calcium is also used to help release hormones and enzymes that affect almost every function in the human body.

BLOOD_PRESSURE_SUMMARY.target: Blood pressure is the force of blood pushing against the walls of the arteries as your heart pumps blood. It includes two measurements. “Systolic” is your blood pressure when your heart beats while pumping blood. “Diastolic” is your blood pressure when the heart is at rest between beats. You usually see blood pressure numbers written with the systolic number above or before the diastolic number (for example, 120/80).

WAIST_CIRCUMFERENCE_SUMMARY.target:
Waist circumference is one metric for assessing risk for obesity-related diseases such as Type 2 diabetes, high cholesterol, high blood pressure, and heart disease.
One way to manage your waist circumference is through healthy eating and exercising. Tracking your results periodically can keep up your motivation to exercise and provide early warnings for important health risks.
To measure, wrap a flexible tape around your waist at the height of your belly button, just above the hips. Don’t hold your breath or hold in your stomach.

STATE_OF_MIND_SUMMARY.target: State of Mind refers to your momentary emotions or daily moods. Keeping a log of your momentary emotions and daily moods can help you identify patterns and reflect on what impacts your state of mind. You can also add context when you log to help you understand which factors are affecting you the most.

SYMPTOM_VOMITING_SUMMARY.target:
Vomiting occurs when the stomach contracts and forces its contents back out of the mouth. Many conditions and situations can bring a need to vomit, ranging from a bumpy car ride or pregnancy to food poisoning and a wide variety of other illnesses.
Most often, the cause is minor and doesn’t require medical attention. But in some cases, the cause can be serious.
Discuss vomiting with a doctor if it persists for more than a day or two, or if it keeps coming back. And get emergency help if it’s accompanied by other symptoms like chest pain, blurred vision, disorientation, high fever, severe headache, or blood in the vomit.

SUGAR_SUMMARY.target:
Sugar is a simple carbohydrate that gives the body energy. The white granulated table sugar you put in your coffee—sucrose from sugar beets or sugar cane—is only one type of sugar. There are many other types, including fructose, found in fruits and honey, and lactose, found in milk. The type of sugar found in our blood, called glucose, is often referred to as “blood sugar.”
Sugar cane was first cultivated in New Guinea about 10,000 years ago.

WALKING_HEART_RATE_AVERAGE_SUMMARY.target:
Your walking heart rate is the average heart beats per minute measured by your Apple Watch during walks at a steady pace throughout the day.
Like resting heart rate, a lower walking heart rate may indicate better heart health and cardiovascular fitness. Increases in walking heart rate at times may be normal and expected, such as during an illness or a pregnancy. Walking regularly has many health benefits, and you may see your walking heart rate lower over time by staying active, managing your weight, and reducing everyday stress.

GAD7_SUMMARY.target:
Anxiety risk refers to an individual’s risk for anxiety-related mental health conditions. This reflects the risk at the time of the most recent mental health assessment score based on the Generalized Anxiety Disorder Questionnaire-7 (GAD-7). The GAD-7 is a tool doctors use to help screen for and measure someone’s anxiety symptoms over a two week period. A mental health questionnaire can be an important part of learning about what’s impacting your mental health. Depending on their family history, biology, or current life events, someone’s anxiety risk may go up or down.
Anxiety is a common and treatable condition. Your anxiety risk is not a diagnosis of any health condition. If you have any questions about your mental health, you should bring them up with a doctor. You can learn more about your current risk for anxiety by taking a mental health questionnaire in Health.

NIACIN_SUMMARY.target: Niacin is a nutrient in the vitamin B complex. The body needs it in small amounts to function and stay healthy. Niacin helps some enzymes work properly and helps the skin, nerves, and digestive tract stay healthy.

VITAMIN_A_SUMMARY.target:
Contributes to healthy skin, teeth, bony and soft tissues, and mucus membranes. Also called retinol, vitamin A gives pigment to the retina and promotes good vision, particularly in poor light.
Dietary sources include eggs, meat, fortified milk, cheese, cream, liver, kidney, and fish oil, or (in the form of beta-carotene) yellow and orange fruits, carrots, pumpkins, sweet potatoes, broccoli, spinach, and most dark green leafy vegetables.

VITAMIN_E_SUMMARY.target:
Vitamin E is an antioxidant that protects against damage caused by free radicals (atoms or molecules made in the body that can damage cells). It also contributes to cardiovascular health.
The best sources of vitamin E are foods such as vegetable oils, nuts, seeds, and green leafy vegetables. Many other foods such as cereals, juices, and margarine are fortified with vitamin E. Vitamin E is fat soluble, so any excess your body doesn’t use is stored for later.

SYMPTOM_CONGESTION_SUMMARY.target:
Congestion in the nose, chest, or ears is characterized by a feeling of obstruction and pressure.
Nasal congestion (a stuffed nose) is caused by the swelling of tissue in the nasal passages rather than something blocking them. This is why blowing your nose provides temporary relief but usually doesn’t fix the problem. It’s most often a symptom of a cold, the flu, or allergies like hay fever. It can also occur during pregnancy due to hormonal fluctuations and increased blood flow.
Chest congestion is generally caused by a buildup of mucus due to an infection. Expectorants can help break mucus up so you can cough it out, but it’s important to know that this only treats the symptom rather than the infection.
Ear congestion is usually a sign of an infection in the ears or sinuses.

AUDIOGRAM_SUMMARY.target:
An audiogram displays the results of a pure-tone audiometry test. It shows how loud sounds need to be in order for you to hear them. The result is an average for each ear based on four frequencies (500Hz, 1kHz, 2kHz, 4kHz).
The difference between the decibel level you need and a normal level indicates your level of hearing impairment. If there’s no difference, your hearing is normal. If there’s some or a lot of difference, your hearing is impaired.

Hearing test results (audiograms) are the result of an audiometry test and show your hearing ability at different frequencies of sound measured in decibels (dbHL). The higher the decibels, the louder a sound needs to be for you to hear it.
Individuals with healthy hearing can hear very soft sounds close to 0 decibels. As people lose their hearing ability, often as they age, sounds have to be louder to be heard. In the test results, the decibels for each frequency can range from -10 (excellent hearing) to over 85 (profound hearing loss).
The average hearing for your left and right ear is based on the four frequencies that are most important for speech (500Hz, 1kHz, 2kHz, 4kHz).

VITAMIN_K_SUMMARY.target:
Vitamin K is essential to blood clotting, and may help maintain bone strength in older persons.
You can get vitamin K by eating foods such as green leafy vegetables (kale, spinach, turnip greens, collards, chard, green-leaf lettuce) or vegetables such as brussels sprouts, broccoli, cauliflower, and cabbage. Some vitamin K is also made by bacteria in your intestine.

SYMPTOM_LOWER_BACK_PAIN_SUMMARY.target:
Back pain can include aching muscles, shooting or stabbing pain, or pain that radiates down your leg.
Most back pain improves within a few weeks with self-care. Dull or aching pain in the lower back can be associated with abdominal cramps due to menstruation. If your pain is severe and doesn’t improve, spreads down your leg, causes weakness or numbness in your legs, or is accompanied by weight loss, you should talk to your doctor. Seek immediate care if your pain causes bowel or bladder problems, is accompanied by a fever, or if it follows a fall or blow to your back.

AUDIO_EXPOSURE_EVENT_SUMMARY.target:
Sounds are generally considered loud when they’re over 80 decibels (dB).
Apple Watch can check the sound levels nearby and notify you when they might affect your hearing. You can manage these notifications in Noise settings on Apple Watch.

CARDIO_FITNESS_SUMMARY.target:
This is a measurement of your VO₂ max, which is the maximum amount of oxygen your body can consume during exercise. Also called cardiorespiratory fitness, this is a useful measurement for everyone from the very fit to those managing illness.
A higher VO₂ max indicates a higher level of cardio fitness and endurance.
Measuring VO₂ max requires a physical test and special equipment. You can also get an estimated VO₂ max with heart rate and motion data from a fitness tracker. Apple Watch can record an estimated VO₂ max when you do a brisk walk, hike, or run outdoors.
VO₂ max is validated for users 20 and older. Most people can improve their VO₂ max with more intense and more frequent cardiovascular exercise. Certain conditions or medications that limit your heart rate may cause an overestimation of your VO₂ max. VO₂ max is not validated for pregnant users. You can indicate you’re taking certain medications or add a current pregnancy in Health Details.

VITAMIN_C_SUMMARY.target:
Vitamin C is a water-soluble vitamin that supports normal growth and development. Vitamin C also helps your body absorb iron. Because your body doesn’t produce or store vitamin C, you need to include it in your diet.
For most people, a large orange or a cup of sliced strawberries, chopped red pepper or broccoli provides enough vitamin C for the day. Any extra vitamin C is flushed out of your body in your urine.

WALKING_STEP_LENGTH_SUMMARY.target:
Step length is the distance between your front foot and back foot when you’re walking. The ability to take longer steps is related to your long term mobility.
Walking requires strength and coordination. Changes in these can affect your ability to take longer steps.
Step length naturally varies with how fast you walk, your height, and the terrain you’re on, but may decline with age, injury, or other factors.
Your iPhone can record step length automatically when you carry your phone near your waist—such as in a pocket—and walk steadily on flat ground. To ensure accuracy, check that your height is up to date in Body Measurements.

FOLATE_SUMMARY.target:
Folate is a B vitamin that helps prevent neural tube defects during pregnancy. It’s important for women of childbearing age to get enough of this vitamin. Folate also helps prevent anemia.
Folate occurs naturally in some foods, such as leafy green vegetables, citrus fruits, and dried beans and peas. The synthetic form of folate, known as folic acid, can be found in fortified cereals and supplements.

SYMPTOM_BODY_ACHE_SUMMARY.target:
Body aches or muscle pain refers to tenderness or soreness within a muscle or throughout the body.
They’re a common symptom of flu and some bacterial infections. And they could indicate a variety of diseases ranging in severity if pain is persistent, felt throughout the body, or accompanied by other troubling symptoms.
The most common causes of muscle pain by far are overexertion or a minor injury. But muscle pain and general body aches can also be caused by factors like stress, dehydration, sleep disruption, or hormonal changes related to menopause.

MAGNESIUM_SUMMARY.target: Magnesium plays a role in many of your body’s chemical processes, and contributes to muscle and nerve function, strong bones, cardiovascular health, and regulated blood sugar. Green leafy vegetables are a great source of magnesium (magnesium is part of chlorophyll, the pigment that makes many plants green).

SPIROMETRY_FVC_SUMMARY.target: Forced vital capacity, a common measure of lung function, is the total amount of air you exhale during a forced expiratory volume test.

EXERCISE_MINUTE_SUMMARY.target: Every full minute of movement equal to or exceeding the intensity of a brisk walk for you counts toward your daily Exercise minutes.

SYMPTOM_PELVIC_PAIN_SUMMARY.target:
There are several types of diseases and conditions that can cause pain in the lowest part of your abdomen and pelvis. It can originate in your digestive, reproductive, or urinary system. It can also come from your muscles, ligaments, or nerves in the pelvis.
Common causes of pelvic pain for both men and women include appendicitis, constipation, irritable bowel syndrome, and kidney stones. Pelvic pain for women can also originate in the reproductive system and can be caused by ovulation, or conditions such as endometriosis, menstrual cramps, ovarian cysts, or uterine fibroids.
If you suddenly feel severe pelvic pain, it might be an emergency and you should consider seeking medical attention. Be sure to get pelvic pain checked by your doctor if it’s new, if it disrupts your daily life, or if it gets worse over time.

SELENIUM_SUMMARY.target: Selenium is a mineral that the body needs to stay healthy. It’s important for reproduction, thyroid function, and DNA production. It also helps protect the body from damage caused by free radicals (atoms or molecules made in the body that can damage cells) and infections. Selenium is present in many foods, and is sometimes added to other foods.

RUNNING_GROUND_CONTACT_TIME_SUMMARY.target:
This is an estimate of the time each foot spends touching the ground while running.
Apple Watch can log your ground contact time automatically during outdoor running workouts.

POTASSIUM_SUMMARY.target:
A type of electrolyte, potassium helps build proteins, break down carbohydrates, build muscle, promote growth, regulate the heart’s electrical activity, and control acidity. Too much or too little (hyper or hypokalemia) can cause abnormal heart rhythms.
Many foods are great sources, including red meats, soy products, milk, yogurt, nuts, citrus fruits, cantaloupes, bananas, apricots (especially dried), broccoli, lima beans, tomatoes, and potatoes (including their skins).

APPLE_BALANCE_METRICS_SUMMARY.target:
This is a collection of measurements, such as heart rate, respiratory rate, and wrist temperature that are taken by Apple Watch while you sleep. Together, these measurements can help you understand how your body is doing. Short-term changes can be a signal that something might be going on.
Each of the metrics is compared to your baseline range. It takes about a week’s worth of sleep sessions to establish your baseline ranges and they’ll continue to refine if you consistently wear your Apple Watch to bed. Make sure your watch isn’t loose on your wrist and that Sleep is on.
A variety of factors can push your vitals out of your typical range, creating an outlier. Caffeine, illness, traveling to higher elevation, exercise, or alcohol are just a few of the factors that can affect your metrics.
Vitals is not designed to detect illness or a medical condition. If you’re concerned about a change in your health, you should speak with a doctor.

ZINC_SUMMARY.target:
This mineral plays an important role in your body’s immune system. After iron, zinc is the most highly concentrated element in the body.
Dietary sources of zinc include high-protein foods such as beef, pork, lamb, dark chicken meat, nuts, whole grains, legumes, and yeast.

SYMPTOM_APPETITE_CHANGES_SUMMARY.target:
A change in appetite is the desire to eat a different amount or type of food than you usually do in your normal eating habits.
This can occur for a number of reasons including stress, changes in activity or diet, nutritional deficits, pregnancy, or menstruation.

STAIR_ASCENT_SPEED_SUMMARY.target:
This is a measurement of how fast you walk up the stairs.
Climbing stairs quickly can be a sign of strong cardiovascular and musculoskeletal health.
Walking up stairs requires strength, coordination, and aerobic fitness. Changes in these factors, or pain, can affect your speed.
Apple Watch records your vertical speed when you go up a flight that is at least 10 feet (3 meters).

BLOOD_ALCOHOL_CONTENT_SUMMARY.target: Blood alcohol content indicates the amount of ethyl alcohol dissolved in your blood. Your blood alcohol level depends upon the rate and amount of alcohol you’ve consumed, as well as your size and weight, your overall health, whether you’ve eaten recently, and the percentage of alcohol in your drinks.

SATURATED_FAT_SUMMARY.target: Saturated fat is found in animal sources of food, such as cheese, red meat, poultry, butter, and whole-milk products. Other foods high in saturated fat include those made with coconut, palm, and other tropical oils. Saturated fat may increase your risk of heart disease and type 2 diabetes.

WALKING_STEADINESS_SUMMARY.target:
This is an estimate of your stability while walking. iPhone calculates Walking Steadiness using your walking speed, step length, double support time, and walking asymmetry data that’s stored in Health. This provides a sense of the way you walk.
Your steadiness is also related to your fall risk. As steadiness goes down, your risk of falling goes up. Walking Steadiness is not an indication of how likely you are to fall in any given moment but an overall sense of fall risk either in the next 12 months, after an injury, or until the end of pregnancy.
iPhone can automatically record your Walking Steadiness in Health when you carry your iPhone in a pocket or holster near your waist. You can also receive a notification if your Walking Steadiness is low or very low. You can manage these notifications in Health Checklist on iPhone.

SYMPTOM_VAGINAL_DRYNESS_SUMMARY.target:
Vaginal dryness is the result of a decrease in the lubrication produced by the cells that line the vagina.
It’s often due to hormonal changes related to menopause, but can also be associated with breastfeeding, certain medications, an infection, high stress, or strenuous exercise.
Persistent dryness can cause itching, burning, and soreness, and can lead to recurring urinary tract infections and pain or bleeding during sex. Medical care should be sought if discomfort is severe or doesn’t go away.

HEADPHONE_AUDIO_EXPOSURE_SUMMARY.target:
This represents the volume of your headphone audio measured in A-weighted decibels (dB). It can be helpful to understand how long you’re exposed to loud audio as this can affect your hearing.
Headphone Audio Levels can be added to Health automatically by your devices. These measurements are most accurate when using Apple or Beats headphones. Audio played through other headphones or speakers connected via a wire can be estimated based on the volume of your device.

SLEEPING_WRIST_TEMPERATURE_SUMMARY.target:
Wrist temperature is a measurement related to your body’s temperature taken by Apple Watch while you’re sleeping. Your data is shown as a change from baseline, an average of recent measurements taken during sleep. While everyone’s wrist temperature baseline is different, tracking nightly changes in your wrist temperature can provide insight into your well-being.
Your body temperature naturally fluctuates, and can vary from night to night due to variables like diet, exercise, and alcohol consumption, or physiological factors like menstrual cycles and illness. Wrist temperature can also be impacted by external factors like your sleep environment. Values within 1.8°F (1°C) of your baseline are common.
Each wrist temperature value is an average of several measurements taken during sleep when Sleep Focus is turned on.

WATER_SUMMARY.target: For your body to function properly, you must replenish its water supply by consuming beverages and foods that contain water. You may need to modify your total fluid intake depending on how active you are, the climate you live in, your health status, and if you’re pregnant or breast-feeding. Food provides about 20 percent of total water intake. Many fruits and vegetables, such as watermelon and spinach, are 90 percent or more water by weight.

SYMPTOM_MEMORY_LAPSE_SUMMARY.target:
A period of time where you forget something you’d normally remember is considered a memory lapse. Lapses in memory or increasing difficulty with words and concepts can be a normal part of aging. There are a number of other potential causes, however. Some of these include consistently disrupted sleep, changes in medication, vitamin deficiencies, anxiety, and depression. Memory issues can also be related to hormonal changes during menopausal transition or menopause itself.
If memory lapses or similar cognitive changes become more frequent or make it hard to perform everyday activities, they may reflect more serious conditions like Alzheimer’s disease.

SODIUM_SUMMARY.target:
Sodium helps maintain the right balance of fluids in your body, helps transmit nerve impulses, and influences muscle contraction and relaxation. Your kidneys naturally balance the amount of sodium stored in your body to maintain optimal health. When your body sodium is low, your kidneys hold on to sodium. When body sodium is high, your kidneys excrete the excess in urine.
Most adults consume much more sodium than is needed. It’s found in many prepared and processed foods, including prepared dinners, cold cuts and bacon, soups, condiments, and fast foods. In addition, many recipes call for salt, and many people also salt their food at the table.

BIOTIN_SUMMARY.target: Biotin, also known as B7, is a vitamin that is found in small amounts in numerous foods. Biotin is an important component of enzymes in the body that break down certain substances like fats and carbohydrates.

SYMPTOM_DIARRHEA_SUMMARY.target:
Multiple bowel movements a day that are watery and thin are considered diarrhea. It usually only lasts for a couple of days but can indicate a serious condition if it lasts longer.
Common causes include sensitivity to certain foods, infection, menstruation, a reaction to medication, surgery, or certain digestive disorders.
Diarrhea can cause dehydration that can be dangerous, especially for children, older adults, or those with weakened immune systems.

CYCLING_POWER_SUMMARY.target:
This is an estimate of the rate of energy used riding a bike and is measured in watts (W). Cycling power is a direct measurement of your work output. It can be affected by factors such as cadence, weight, and fitness level.
Cycling power can be automatically collected by a sensor during cycling workouts and logged to Health.

VISION_PRESCRIPTION_SUMMARY.target:
A vision prescription is a record of your eyes’ ability to see and their measurements. This is often based on an eye exam with an eye care professional.
The data recorded in the prescription can provide a lens maker with the information needed to create corrective eyewear such as glasses or contacts.
A vision prescription can be added to Health manually.

SYMPTOM_NIGHT_SWEATS_SUMMARY.target:
Night sweats refer to sweating during sleep that’s not caused by external factors like heavy blankets or a warm room.
Common causes include certain medications such as antidepressants, an infection, low blood sugar, hormonal disorders like hypothyroidism, and normal hormonal changes related to menopause.
If accompanied by weight loss or fever, night sweats could indicate a health condition requiring medical attention.

SYMPTOM_SLEEP_CHANGES_SUMMARY.target:
These are changes in the length or quality of your sleep and are not caused by known, external factors. Sleep changes are more common as you get older.
Consistent sleep can improve focus, concentration, and general well-being. Going to sleep and waking up at the same time each day can make it easier to fall asleep and stay asleep.
If you have ongoing problems with your sleep, it may be a sign of insomnia.

CHROMIUM_SUMMARY.target: Chromium promotes synthesis of the fatty acids and cholesterol needed for brain function and other bodily processes. The best source of chromium is brewer’s yeast, but other good sources are beef, liver, eggs, chicken, oysters, wheat germ, green peppers, apples, bananas, spinach, black pepper, and molasses.

SLEEP_BREATHING_DISTURBANCES_SUMMARY.target:
Breathing disturbances are short, temporary interruptions of your breathing pattern while you’re asleep. They’re fairly common and people typically experience a few disturbances a night.
Body position, alcohol intake, upper respiratory illnesses, and even some medications can lead to increased breathing disturbances on a night-to-night basis.
An elevated number of disturbances for multiple nights may indicate a condition called sleep apnea.
When turned on, Apple Watch can track your breathing disturbances each night and categorize them as Not Elevated or Elevated.
If you’re diagnosed with sleep apnea, you should not make any changes to your treatments without talking to your doctor first.

SYMPTOM_BLOATING_SUMMARY.target:
Bloating is a feeling of tightness, discomfort, or fullness in your stomach or abdomen. It is often the result of intestinal gas and can be due to your diet, various bowel issues, or menstruation.
On very rare occasions, severe or constant bloating may signify more serious conditions like fluid in the abdomen, bowel obstruction, or ovarian cancer.

SIX_MINUTE_WALK_TEST_DISTANCE_SUMMARY.target:
This is an estimate of how far you can walk on flat ground in six minutes based on your recent motion and workout data. The more fit you are, the higher this number will be.
This prediction is considered a measure of your capacity for exercise. Longer distances are associated with healthier cardiac, respiratory, circulatory, and neuromuscular function, and may reflect your ability to perform every day activities. Improvements in fitness and mobility can increase your six-minute walk distance.
The standard six-minute walk test measures the maximum number of meters you can walk on an unobstructed, flat course doing laps of a standard length. The test is often given to those who are recovering from a cardiac or respiratory condition. You can get a predicted six-minute walk distance up to 500 meters using data from a device, such as Apple Watch.

BLOOD_GLUCOSE_SUMMARY.target:
Also called blood sugar, this is a form of sugar that your body can absorb after breaking down the food you eat. Glucose is the body’s most common source of energy.
People with diabetes often track their glucose levels in order to manage their condition. If you don’t have diabetes, knowing your levels over time can help you understand your risk.
Blood glucose values can be added to Health manually or automatically by a Bluetooth meter.

SYMPTOM_FATIGUE_SUMMARY.target:
Fatigue is a feeling of tiredness often due to mental or physical effort. Temporary fatigue usually has an obvious cause and likely remedy. Resting relieves tiredness in most cases.
Ongoing exhaustion is more profound and isn’t relieved by rest. A nearly constant state of fatigue can reduce your energy, motivation, and concentration. Tiredness at this level can also impact your emotional and psychological well-being.
Fatigue can occur for many reasons including menstruation, certain medications and medical conditions such as anemia, hypothyroidism, sleep apnea, or specific vitamin deficiencies.

STAIR_DESCENT_SPEED_SUMMARY.target:
This is a measurement of how fast you walk down the stairs.
Descending stairs safely is an important indicator of your overall mobility.
Descending stairs requires strength and coordination. Changes in these factors, or pain, can affect your speed.
Apple Watch records your vertical speed when you go down a flight that is at least 10 feet (3 meters).

PREGNANCY_SUMMARY.target:
Pregnancy begins with the fertilization of an egg by a sperm and the implantation of the fertilized egg in the uterus.
A pregnancy that continues to full term will result in the delivery of an infant about forty weeks after the first day of the last menstrual period, either through vaginal delivery or cesarean section.
Complications that arise during pregnancy can lead to a miscarriage, or to a condition that is dangerous for the pregnant person, the fetus, or both. While fatigue and nausea are common during a healthy pregnancy, vaginal bleeding or severe pain can signal a problem and should be discussed with a doctor promptly.
Menstrual cycles stop during pregnancy. For most people who lactate, the return of menstruation may be delayed for several months after delivery.

HEART_RATE_SUMMARY.target:
Your heart beats approximately 100,000 times per day, accelerating and slowing through periods of rest and exertion. Your heart rate refers to how many times your heart beats per minute and can be an indicator of your cardiovascular health.
Health visualizes a history of the heart rate data collected by Apple Watch or a heart rate monitor so you can see your patterns and variability over time and with different activities.

SLEEP_ANALYSIS_SUMMARY.target:
Sleep provides insight into your sleep habits. Sleep trackers and monitors can help you determine the amount of time you are in bed and asleep. These devices estimate your time in bed and your time asleep by analyzing changes in physical activity, including movement during the night. You can also keep track of your sleep by entering your own estimation of your bed time and sleep time manually.
The “In Bed” period reflects the time period you are lying in bed with the intention to sleep. For most people it starts when you turn the lights off and it ends when you get out of bed. The “Asleep” period reflects the period(s) you are asleep.

NIKE_FUEL_SUMMARY.target:
NikeFuel is a single, universal way to measure whole body movement. NikeFuel removes all personal differences from the equation—like age, gender, body weight or physical fitness level—and focuses simply on the energy required to perform an activity.
NikeFuel makes it easy to compare, compete and collaborate across athlete populations, sports and life. NikeFuel measures both all day activity as well as training intensity, providing athletes with real time feedback and guidance across any sport, at any skill level.

INSULIN_DELIVERY_SUMMARY.target:
Insulin is a hormone that allows your body to process blood glucose into energy. People with insulin-dependent diabetes inject or infuse one or more forms of this hormone to regulate their blood glucose.
Tracking Insulin Delivery can help promote consistent habits and reveal underlying trends — especially when considered in the context of blood glucose and activity data.

SYMPTOM_DRY_SKIN_SUMMARY.target:
When the top layer of skin loses too much moisture, it can cause scaling, cracking, or itching. A variety of conditions including diabetes and hypothyroidism can lead to persistently dry skin. It’s also common during menopause due to a decline in the hormone estrogen.
If dry skin is becoming painful, or if skin is so dry it is bleeding or getting infections, this may need to be examined by a doctor.

RESPIRATORY_RATE_SUMMARY.target:
Also commonly called respiration rate or breathing rate, this refers to the number of times you breathe in a minute.
When you inhale, your lungs fill with air and oxygen is added to your blood stream while carbon dioxide is removed from your blood. The carbon dioxide is then released from your lungs as you exhale.
Your respiratory rate can increase when your body needs more oxygen, such as when you’re exercising. It can also decrease when you need less—during sleep for example.

PREGNANCY_TEST_RESULT_SUMMARY.target:
A pregnancy test can detect a particular hormone produced by a pregnancy. A positive pregnancy test means that this hormone is present and you are pregnant. A negative pregnancy test can mean that you are not pregnant, or that you are too early in a pregnancy for the test to measure the hormone.
This test can help you detect a pregnancy early and can be useful information when talking to your doctor.
Your Pregnancy Test Result may vary depending on how soon you take the test after a pregnancy starts.

FIBER_SUMMARY.target: Dietary fiber (also called roughage) is plant matter that humans can’t digest. Even though your body doesn’t absorb fiber, it’s good for you in other ways. In addition to helping you feel fuller with fewer calories, fiber helps keep your digestive tract working well. Fiber is found only in plant products; most fruits, vegetables, and whole grains are high in fiber.

VITAMIN_D_SUMMARY.target:
Vitamin D helps your body absorb calcium. Calcium is one of the main building blocks of bone. A lack of vitamin D can lead to bone diseases such as osteoporosis or rickets. Vitamin D also has a role in your nerve, muscle, and immune systems.
You can get vitamin D in three ways: through your skin, from your diet, and from supplements. Your body forms vitamin D naturally after exposure to sunlight. However, too much sun exposure can lead to skin aging and skin cancer, so many people try to get their vitamin D from other sources.
Vitamin D–rich foods include egg yolks, saltwater fish, and liver. Some other foods, like milk and cereal, often have added vitamin D. You can also take vitamin D supplements. Check with your health care provider to see how much you should take.

SYMPTOM_FAINTING_SUMMARY.target:
Fainting is the temporary loss of consciousness, usually resulting from an insufficient flow of blood, oxygen, or glucose to the brain.
It’s often preceded by dizziness, nausea, tingling, impaired vision, or impaired hearing. Reasons for a fainting episode are often benign, but can be urgent.
Fainting brought on by intense stress, fear, or pain (vasovagal syncope) is rarely dangerous once consciousness returns. Potentially more serious causes include heart conditions, seizures, or anemia. Fainting can also result from medications that lower blood pressure, and can sometimes occur during pregnancy when blood vessels near the heart become partially compressed.

CYCLING_CADENCE_SUMMARY.target:
This represents the number of times you turn the pedals over in a minute while riding a bike. It’s measured in revolutions per minute, or RPMs. Cadence can be affected by many factors such as incline, resistance, and fitness level.
Cycling cadence can be automatically collected by a sensor during cycling workouts and logged to Health.

CHOLESTEROL_SUMMARY.target: Cholesterol is a fat-like substance found in all cells of the body. It’s used to make hormones, vitamin D, and substances that help you digest foods. Your body makes all the cholesterol it needs, but you get extra cholesterol when you eat foods such as meats, liver and other organ meats, dairy foods, egg yolks, and shellfish.

DIETARY_ENERGY_SUMMARY.target:
Dietary energy is the energy in food. Your body has a constant demand for energy and uses the energy from food to fuel your every action, from fidgeting to running. Your body also uses energy for basic functions such as breathing, digestion, and blood circulation.
Dietary energy is either converted to physical energy or stored within your body as fat, protein, and carbohydrates. This stored energy remains in your body unless you use it up, either by reducing energy intake so that your body must draw on reserves for energy, or by increasing physical activity so that you burn more energy.

SYMPTOM_MOOD_CHANGES_SUMMARY.target:
Changes in your emotions, energy levels, or focus that affect your ability to work, study, interact with family or friends, or do normal daily activities.
Understanding if there’s a pattern to your mood changes can help you identify causes and ways to deal with them. Mood changes that last for months can be a sign of an underlying disorder such as anxiety or depression.
Mood changes and Menstruation:
It’s common to have mood changes around your period. Changes that are not caused by external factors may be a sign of pre-menstrual syndrome or a more severe form known as pre-menstrual dysphoric disorder.
Mood changes can be logged manually as part of Cycle Tracking.

SYMPTOM_COUGHING_SUMMARY.target:
A cough is a reflex the body uses to get rid of irritants, triggered by the stimulation of nerve endings in the throat or airways.
Sometimes it’s caused by food caught in the throat or inhaled particles. It can also occur when nerve endings are irritated by inflammation from an infection or disease.
The characteristics of a cough can help determine its cause. Characteristics include: degree of pain; sound; whether or not it produces mucus; what triggers bring it on; how long it lasts; and other symptoms like fever, runny nose, nausea, or difficulty breathing.
Common causes include: respiratory ailments like cold, flu, bronchitis, croup, or pertussis; inhaled particles like dust, smoke, or pollen; inflammation such as tonsillitis; or other serious conditions like lung cancer or emphysema.

HEART_RATE_VARIABILITY_SUMMARY.target: Heart Rate Variability (HRV) is a measure of the variation in the time interval between heart beats. Apple Watch calculates HRV by using the standard deviation of beat-to-beat measurements which are captured by the heart rate sensor. HRV is validated for users over the age of 18. Third party apps and devices can also add HRV to Health.

PHYSICAL_EFFORT_SUMMARY.target:
Physical Effort is an estimate of the energy you’re using to perform a task excluding other factors such as temperature, altitude, or heart rate. This makes Physical Effort a good indicator of your overall effort and intensity levels when it comes to exercise and other day-to-day activities. It’s measured in METs which stands for metabolic equivalent of task. One MET represents the energy you use when you’re not moving and calm. If you go for a bike ride, you’d likely use eight times more energy than you do sitting quietly which equals eight METs. You might use five METs walking briskly or two METs washing dishes.
Physical Effort can be estimated and recorded automatically by Apple Watch.

STAND_HOUR_SUMMARY.target: A “stand hour” represents an hour in your day where you stood and moved around a little for at least one minute. THIAMIN_SUMMARY.target: Also known as vitamin B1, thiamin helps your body convert carbohydrates into energy. Thiamin deficiency, often a result of alcohol abuse, can lead to fatigue and, in extreme cases, beriberi.

SYMPTOM_SKIPPED_HEARTBEAT_SUMMARY.target:
A skipped heartbeat is a sensation in your chest that feels like a missed or abnormal heartbeat, also known as a palpitation. There may, or may not, be an actual underlying missed heartbeat. Most of the time, occasional sensations of skipped heartbeats occur without abnormal heart activity and are not concerning. Typically, this is related to exercise, stress, or excessive caffeine.
If palpitations happen frequently, there may be an underlying abnormal heartbeat such as a premature ventricular contraction (PVC) or another cardiac arrhythmia. Stress, anxiety, stimulants, or hormone changes can cause recurring symptoms. If these symptoms appear repeatedly, they should be discussed with a doctor, especially if they’re accompanied by other symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness, or disorientation.

SYMPTOM_ACNE_SUMMARY.target:
Also called pimples or zits, acne is a skin condition that occurs when follicles are plugged with oil and dead skin cells. Acne can occur anywhere on the body but generally appear on the face, back, or chest.
It’s very common in young adults and usually improves with age. When associated with menstruation, acne tends to occur just before or during a period. There are different kinds of acne with some being more severe than others, and scarring can occur with the most severe forms.

PANTOTHENIC_ACID_SUMMARY.target: Pantothenic acid, also called vitamin B5, aids in metabolism (the breakdown and use of food). It’s water soluble, so excess is eliminated and you need a fresh supply every day. Get it in your diet by eating foods rich in vitamin B, such as sweet potatoes, mushrooms, and cauliflower.

WALKING_DOUBLE_SUPPORT_PERCENTAGE_SUMMAR.target:
This is the percentage of time during a walk that both feet are on the ground. A lower value means you spend more of your walk with your weight on one foot instead of two, which can be a sign of better balance. During a typical walk, this measure will fall between 20 to 40%.
Walking requires strength and coordination. Changes in these can affect your balance and two-foot contact time.
Double support time naturally varies with how fast you walk and terrain, but may increase with age.
Double support time is recorded automatically on iPhone when you carry your phone near your waist, such as in a pants pocket, and walk steadily over flat ground.

MENSTRUAL_CYCLE_DEVIATION_SPOTTING_SUMMA.target:
Persistent spotting, also known as irregular intermenstrual bleeding, is defined as spotting that occurs in at least two of your cycles in the last six months. Persistent spotting may be a sign of underlying medical conditions such as infections, polyps, or in some cases, cancer.
Cycle Tracking can detect persistent spotting using your tracked flow and spotting days.

CONTRACEPTIVE_SUMMARY.target:
Contraceptives, also known as birth control, are devices, medications, or techniques used to prevent pregnancy. Several types are commonly used and work in different ways. The main ways to prevent pregnancy are to stop an egg from being released, or keep the sperm from reaching an egg.
Some contraceptive methods, like condoms, diaphragms, and cervical caps, create a physical barrier to stop sperm from reaching an egg. Others, like spermicides, block sperm entry into the cervix by reducing sperm’s ability to move. Condoms are the only birth control method that also helps protect against sexually transmitted diseases.
Many contraceptives use the hormones estrogen and progesterone to disrupt ovulation and make it harder for sperm to reach eggs that are released during ovulation. The hormones are taken orally with a pill, absorbed through the skin from a patch, or delivered via injection or implanted device.
One type of intrauterine device (IUD) uses copper rather than hormones to prevent sperm from fertilizing eggs.
Fertility awareness based methods such as standard days method, prevent pregnancy by avoiding intercourse during potential fertile windows in your menstrual cycle. These methods require close attention to where you are in your menstrual cycle, as well as changes in cervical mucus or basal body temperature. Sterilization, both male and female, are permanent forms of contraception that require a procedure.
These methods vary in the effort required, how long they last, and how effective they are in preventing pregnancy.

MENSTRUAL_CYCLE_DEVIATION_PROLONGED_SUMM.target:
Prolonged periods are defined as menstrual bleeding that lasts for ten or more days, and this has happened at least two times in the last six months. Persistent prolonged periods may be a sign of underlying medical conditions such as fibroids or adenomyosis, a condition where the uterine lining grows into the surrounding muscles.
Cycle Tracking can detect prolonged periods using your tracked flow days.

VITAMIN_B12_SUMMARY.target: Vitamin B12 helps keep the body’s nerve and blood cells healthy. It helps make DNA, the genetic material in all cells. INTERMENSTRUAL_BLEEDING_SUMMARY.target: Spotting is light vaginal bleeding, usually not enough to cover a panty liner. Spotting may happen sporadically in between periods. CARBOHYDRATES_SUMMARY.target: Carbohydrates are used by the body to make glucose—the fuel that gives you energy. Carbohydrates occur in a variety of forms: simple sugars, more complex starches, and fiber. Most natural unprocessed foods—vegetables, fruits, legumes, and whole grains, for example—are rich in carbohydrates. Other foods like white rice, white bread, cakes, and cookies also contain carbohydrates, often in the form of starch or sugar.

OVULATION_TEST_RESULT_SUMMARY.target:
Ovulation tests can predict how likely you are to ovulate. A positive or peak result means you should ovulate soon. High means you probably have increased fertility. Negative or low means you’re unlikely to ovulate soon.
Tracking Ovulation Test Results can provide an understanding of your hormones and ovulation during each cycle. This information can be useful for fertility planning or when talking to your doctor.

SYMPTOM_ABDOMINAL_CRAMPS_SUMMARY.target:
This is a dull aching or sharp pain in your abdomen that comes and goes. The most common causes are digestive issues like a reaction to certain foods (e.g. lactose intolerance), gas, constipation, or diarrhea. Cramps are also one of the most common menstrual complaints.
If your pain is recurring, it may be due to gall stones, irritable bowel syndrome, inflammatory bowel disease, or another chronic abdominal condition. If the pain is sudden, severe, or is associated with other symptoms like fever or fatigue, it may be a serious acute condition. This could include appendicitis, bowel obstruction, kidney stones, or a kidney infection.

CAFFEINE_SUMMARY.target: Caffeine is a stimulant found in coffee, tea, soft drinks, chocolate, kola nuts, and some medicines. Modest amounts can make you more alert, but too much can make you jittery and make it hard to sleep.

IODINE_SUMMARY.target: Iodine is a mineral found in some foods. Your body needs iodine to make thyroid hormones. These hormones control your body’s metabolism and other functions. They are also important for bone and brain development during pregnancy and infancy.

SLEEP_APNEA_EVENT_SUMMARY.target:
Sleep apnea is a respiratory condition where you experience repeated disturbances in breathing while asleep.
While a few disturbances on a given night can be common, an elevated level of breathing disturbances over multiple nights can indicate you have sleep apnea.
When notifications are turned on, Apple Watch can track your breathing disturbances each night and categorize them as Not Elevated or Elevated.
If those breathing disturbances over a 30 day period are suggestive of sleep apnea Apple Watch can notify you.
Consistent measurements are needed to identify sleep apnea so you should wear your watch to sleep every night.

SYMPTOM_FEVER_SUMMARY.target:
Any orally-measured body temperature above 100.4°F is generally considered a fever. Measurements in the armpit tend to be slightly lower and rectal measurements tend to be slightly higher than oral measurements.
Usually a fever is the result of heat generated by the immune system to fight an infection or other perceived threat. Depending on the cause, fever may be accompanied by other symptoms like chills, sweating, head or body aches, weakness, nausea, and loss of appetite.
In addition to viral or bacterial infection, other causes of fever include autoimmune diseases like lupus or rheumatoid arthritis, certain medications and immunizations, heat stroke, and hormone disorders.

SYMPTOM_HEADACHE_SUMMARY.target:
A headache is pain in any part of the head. Pain may occur on one or both sides of the head, be isolated to a certain location, radiate from one point, or feel like pressure.
It can feel like a sharp pain, throbbing, or a dull ache. Headaches can develop quickly or gradually and last less than an hour to several days. Migraines are a type of intense headache that are often accompanied by nausea or sensitivity to light or sound.

ACTIVITY_SUMMARY_SUMMARY_PAIRED_WATCH_WH.target: Activity rings on Apple Watch give you a quick visual reference of your daily activity using three metrics: Roll, Move, and Exercise. When you complete your daily goal for each metric, its ring closes. Roll measures how often you take a break and push around over the course of the day. Move measures how many active calories you burn. Exercise measures how many minutes of brisk activity you do. Visit the Activity app on your Apple Watch to get started.

RESTING_HEART_RATE_SUMMARY.target:
Your resting heart rate is the average heart beats per minute measured when you’ve been inactive or relaxed for several minutes. A lower resting heart rate typically indicates better heart health and cardiovascular fitness. An increase in resting heart rate at times may be normal and expected, such as during an illness or a pregnancy.
You may be able to lower your resting heart rate over time by staying active, managing your weight, and reducing everyday stress. Resting heart rate does not include your heart rate while you’re asleep and is validated for users over the age of 18.

VO2_MAX_SUMMARY.target:
VO₂ max is the maximum amount of oxygen your body can consume during exercise. Also called cardiorespiratory fitness, this is a useful measurement for everyone from the very fit to those managing illness.
A higher VO₂ max indicates a higher level of cardio fitness and endurance.
Measuring VO₂ max requires a physical test and special equipment. You can also get an estimated VO₂ max with heart rate and motion data from a fitness tracker. Apple Watch can record an estimated VO₂ max when you do a brisk walk, hike, or run outdoors.
VO₂ max is validated for users 20 and older. Most people can improve their VO₂ max with more intense and more frequent cardiovascular exercise. Certain conditions or medications that limit your heart rate may cause an overestimation of your VO₂ max.

BODY_MASS_INDEX_SUMMARY.target: Body Mass Index (BMI) is an indicator of your body fat. It’s calculated from your height and weight, and can tell you whether you are underweight, normal, overweight, or obese. It can also help you gauge your risk for diseases that can occur with more body fat.

RIBOFLAVIN_SUMMARY.target: Riboflavin is a water-soluble B vitamin important for growth and red blood cell production. Get your supply by eating foods that are high in vitamin B.

CYCLING_SPEED_SUMMARY.target:
This is a measurement of how fast you are traveling while riding a bike, calculated as distance over time. It can be used to estimate the intensity of your activity. Your cycling speed can be affected by many factors such as wind resistance, incline, surface, and the type of bike you’re riding.
Cycling speed can be measured by a sensor and logged after a cycling workout by an app that adds workouts to Health.

TOTAL_FAT_SUMMARY.target: Total fat is the amount of all fats consumed—saturated, unsaturated (monounsaturated and polyunsaturated), and trans fats. Fats are one of the body’s three sources of energy, along with carbohydrates and proteins.

IRON_SUMMARY.target: Iron is a mineral that (among other things) helps transport oxygen throughout the body. Iron deficiency may lead to anemia, cause fatigue, and impair other functions. Lean meats, poultry, fish, beans, legumes, and dark green leafy vegetables are some good dietary iron sources. Eating foods rich in vitamin C at the same time can help your body absorb iron.

ATRIAL_FIBRILLATION_BURDEN_SUMMARY.target:
This represents how often your heart is in atrial fibrillation (AFib), a common irregular rhythm. It can help you understand if your AFib is becoming more or less frequent and if life factors, such as exercise or sleep, have an impact on it.
If you’re already diagnosed with AFib, Apple Watch can track your heart rhythm and the Health app can estimate your AFib History each week. The percentage estimate is based on seven days of readings taken by Apple Watch and does not indicate if your heart is in AFib at any given moment.
Do not make any changes to your medications without discussing those changes with your doctor first.
Apple Watch cannot detect a heart attack or stroke.

TIME_IN_DAYLIGHT_SUMMARY.target:
Time in Daylight is an estimate of the amount of time spent in sunlight. For children, spending 80-120 minutes outside each day can help lower the risk for myopia or nearsightedness. For adults, spending around 20 minutes outdoors every day has numerous physical and mental health benefits.
Time outside allows your eyes to focus on objects farther away, reducing eye strain associated with working on something close, such as a screen or sketchbook. Sunlight also helps your body produce vitamin D, which your body needs to absorb calcium, protect your bones, teeth, and muscles and support your immune system.
When unobstructed, Apple Watch can automatically record an estimated amount of Time in Daylight in Health.

HEART_RATE_RECOVERY_SUMMARY.target:
Often called heart rate recovery, this is an estimate of how quickly your heart rate could drop after you reach your peak heart rate during exercise. It’s estimated by tracking the change in your heart rate one minute after you stop exercising. The higher your value of Cardio Recovery, the better. It can be an indicator of your cardiovascular health.
Measuring your cardio recovery can be done in a lab setting on a treadmill or a stationary bike. It can also be estimated using data Apple Watch records during and after several outdoor walking, outdoor running, or hiking workouts. Your heart rate does not have to reach its peak in order to estimate your recovery.

SYMPTOM_SHORTNESS_OF_BREATH_SUMMARY.target:
This is the feeling that you can’t catch your breath. It may feel like a sensation of tightness in the chest that makes it hard to fully expand the lungs and fill them with air.
It’s most often the result of strenuous activity or environmental factors like high temperatures, poor air quality, or being at high altitude. In these circumstances, shortness of breath can be more pronounced for people with certain health issues like obesity, hypertension, or diseases of the heart or lungs.
Even without changes in activity or environment, those conditions and others like anxiety or allergies can cause difficulty breathing. Anyone experiencing severe shortness of breath should seek immediate medical care—especially if it comes on suddenly, doesn’t go away with a few minutes of rest, or is accompanied by other symptoms like chest pain, disorientation, fever, or a blue color in the lips or nails.

SYMPTOM_BREAST_PAIN_SUMMARY.target:
There are two types of breast pain: cyclic and noncyclic.
Cyclic pain is caused by hormone changes during the menstrual cycle. It’s typically described as a dull, heavy, or aching sensation and often occurs just before or during your period. It typically affects both breasts and can radiate out to under the arms. Cyclic breast pain is more likely to affect younger women who haven’t experienced menopause yet.
Noncyclic pain is often described as tightness, soreness, or a burning sensation. It can be constant or come and go and typically affects an area of one of the breasts. It can spread across a breast. This kind of pain is most likely to come after menopause.
Breast pain rarely indicates cancer. If your breast pain doesn’t go away after one or two menstrual cycles or persists after menopause, you should bring it up with your doctor.

BODY_TEMPERATURE_SUMMARY.target:
Normal body temperature varies throughout the day—it’s lower in the morning and higher in the late afternoon and evening. The average normal body temperature is 98.6°F (37°C). What’s normal for you may be a degree or more higher or lower than this.
Body temperature can be affected by many factors, including heavy exercise, outdoor heat and humidity, and menstrual cycles. Of course, your body temperature may also rise if you have an illness. This is known as a fever.

SYMPTOM_CONSTIPATION_SUMMARY.target:
Constipation is generally described as difficulty passing stool, often with infrequent bowel movements—fewer than three in a week. Bowel movements may even be painful with small, firm stool.
Constipation is commonly caused by a low fiber diet, low activity levels, dehydration, certain medications, or decreased gut movement that comes with age.

SYMPTOM_HAIR_LOSS_SUMMARY.target:
Gradual hair loss is a common effect of aging, with hair usually receding from the front and top of the head for men and thinning for women.
Other factors that can contribute to hair loss include stress, illness, diet, exercise routine, medication or hypothyroidism.
Hormonal changes related to menopause or pregnancy can also lead to the slowed growth, thinning, and loss of hair. A decline in estrogen and progesterone along with an increase in male hormones called androgens, can shrink hair follicles and stimulate the growth of hair on the face.

SYMPTOM_LOSS_OF_TASTE_SUMMARY.target:
Loss of the sense of taste is the inability to distinguish flavors. Loss of taste most often results from loss of smell, because the taste receptors in the mouth only detect saltiness, sweetness, or bitterness. Our sense of smell is what allows us to taste specific flavors.
Partial or complete loss of smell and taste often occur with aging, and also commonly result from allergies like hay fever and infections like a cold or flu. Other causes include smoking, a deviated septum, and injuries or diseases affecting the brain.
Loss of taste doesn’t always come from an issue with smell. Certain medications can cause it. So can damage to taste receptors from burning or chemical exposure. If the damage isn’t severe, taste usually returns. Bad oral hygiene or dental problems can also impair taste.

SYMPTOM_HEARTBURN_SUMMARY.target:
Heartburn is a painful burning sensation in the chest and upper belly that usually arises when acid escapes from the stomach and irritates the esophagus.
Usually the cause is not serious and can be relieved with over-the-counter medication. If you experience frequent and persistent heartburn, you may have gastrointestinal reflux disease (GERD). Left untreated, GERD can damage the esophagus.
Heartburn can also occur in people who are obese or pregnant, when acid is pushed into the esophagus by pressure on the stomach.
If accompanied by other symptoms such as chest pressure or difficulty breathing, heartburn can be a sign of a heart attack and medical assistance should be sought immediately.
